title: Asbestos Safety and Eradication Agency Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish a national Asbestos Safety and Eradication Agency to coordinate the strategic plan for asbestos awareness, removal and management across Australia.
The Agency would consist of a chief executive and staff, supported by a Council advising the chief executive and Minister on asbestos safety.
Its functions would include coordination with governments, research and reporting on implementation of the National Strategic Plan, with the legislation extending to external Territories.
changes: The Agency would need an annual operational plan approved by the Minister.
The chief executive would have to consider the Council's advice, recommendations and guidelines.
The Council could advise the chief executive but could not give directions.
A review of the Agency's role and functions would begin five years after commencement and finish within six months.
summary.affected: Agency staff and Council members, including representatives of Commonwealth, State, Territory and local governments, are affected.

speeches.speaker: Sussan Ley
speeches.brief: Supported the Asbestos Safety and Eradication Agency Bill 2013, citing continuing asbestos risks, fragmented regulation and the need for all levels of government to participate, while questioning funding of $10½ million compared with $12.3 million.

speeches.speaker: Daryl Melham
speeches.brief: Supported the Asbestos Safety and Eradication Agency Bill 2013, urged education warnings for home renovators, reported community and personal impacts of asbestos disease, and called for research, prevention and cross-party action.

speeches.speaker: Bill Shorten
speeches.brief: Introduced the Asbestos Safety and Eradication Agency Bill 2013 to implement the Asbestos Management Review's recommendations, citing International Labour Organization figures that someone worldwide dies of an asbestos-related disease every five minutes, and said the first national strategic plan for asbestos eradication is due by 1 July this year.

speeches.speaker: Eric Abetz
speeches.brief: The Asbestos Safety and Eradication Agency Bill 2013 was supported, establishing a national agency to coordinate asbestos safety and eradication, with Australia facing an estimated 13,000 mesothelioma cases by 2020 and 40,000 other asbestos-related cancers. The coalition criticised a $1.8 million funding cut from the originally pledged $12.3 million to $10.5 million, and urged broader state representation on the agency's council and expanded research functions.
